idiom_name: dirty map + flush goroutine (channel/ticker) over database/sql transactions
implementation_notes: database/sql gives you transactions (DB.BeginTx and sql.Tx) but no persistence context, so the accumulator is yours: a map keyed by row id guarded by sync.Mutex (or owned outright by the flusher goroutine), fed by a wake-up channel and drained by a flusher that selects on the channel plus a time.Ticker and executes the batch through one transaction. What replaces the classic structure: nothing at the ORM level - the goroutine/channel pair is the idiomatic substitute for a flush thread, and Tx.StmtContext/prepared statements remove per-write parse cost. Justified when write throughput matters; for low-volume CRUD, write straight through.
pitfalls: Go maps are not safe for concurrent writes: guard the dirty map with a mutex or give it to a single goroutine, otherwise staging races with the flusher.
A deferred Tx.Rollback after a failed Commit hides the real error unless the commit error is checked and returned first.
An unbuffered wake-up channel blocks producers while the flusher works - use the non-blocking send shown above so staging never stalls.
